source_text: Qui et crimina voluntatis ignovit, a quibus liberum fuerat abstinere, et sui imitatione, qui erat virtutum forma et norma, correctis gloriam beatae aeternitatis indulsit. Cum ergo utramque nationem pro voluminis sui tempore et iure conveniat, in his tamen locis, de quibus quaestio est, cum Israelitis omnino manum conserit, qui audebant de praeputiorum stirpe venientes eo usque despicere ut affirmarent eos nec suffragio fidei ad consortium suum transire potuisse; contra quod supercilium replicat Iudaeae gentis exordia et in ipsa radice circumcisionis ostendit non tanti esse praeputium, ut aut iniustos eius relictio aut iustos faciat eius ablatio.
pass_a_gloss: Who both pardoned the crimes of will, from which it had been free to abstain, and by imitation of himself, who was a form and norm of virtues, indulged to the corrected the glory of a blessed eternity. When therefore he convenes each nation according to the time and right of his volume, nevertheless in these places about which the question is he altogether joins hand with the Israelites, who were daring so far to despise those coming from the stock of foreskins as to affirm that they could not even by the vote of faith have passed into their consortium; against which eyebrow he unfolds the beginnings of the Jewish nation and in the very root of circumcision shows that the foreskin is not of so much, that either its leaving make unjust or its taking-away make just.

lemmas.lexica: LS imitatio; Blaise moral copying vs generation of sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere

pass_b_english: Christ both forgave the will’s crimes, from which they had been free to abstain, and granted the glory of blessed eternity to those corrected by imitation of him, the model and rule of virtues. Although Paul addresses both nations as the course and demands of his book require, in these disputed passages he is engaged entirely with the Israelites. They dared to despise those coming from uncircumcised stock so thoroughly that they asserted these people could not enter their fellowship even through the support of faith. Against this arrogance he recounts the Jewish people’s beginnings and shows, at the very root of circumcision, that the foreskin is not so important that leaving it makes people unjust or removing it makes them just.

choices.why: Julian's Rom 5:12 reading: sin passes by copying Adam's example, not by generation/seed.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
